subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 26-year-old mountaineer rapidly ascends from sea level to an altitude of 4,200 m and develops headache, dyspnea, and fatigue. His oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry is 84%, and arterial blood gas shows a normal PaCO2 with mild respiratory alkalosis. After 4 days of acclimatization his resting ventilation is higher, his hemoglobin is 16.8 g/dL, and his hemoglobin P50 has increased from 26 to 30 mm Hg.
question: Which of the following changes is most responsible for the rightward shift of the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve in this patient?

options.text: Increased carbon monoxide binding to heme iron
Oxidation of heme iron from Fe2+ to Fe3+

explanation_correct: At high altitude, chronic hypoxia increases glycolysis in erythrocytes and raises 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate, which binds deoxyhemoglobin and stabilizes the T state of the tetramer. This right shifts the dissociation curve (higher P50) and improves oxygen unloading to tissues despite the lower arterial oxygen saturation; the shift is summarized by the CADET mnemonic (CO2, acid, 2,3-DPG, exercise, temperature).

explanation_incorrect.A: A fall in 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate removes the T-state stabilizer and shifts the curve to the left, increasing oxygen affinity and impairing tissue unloading, the opposite of what is observed after acclimatization.
explanation_incorrect.B: Carbon monoxide binds ferrous heme with roughly 200-fold greater affinity than oxygen and left shifts the remaining binding sites; it does not explain the adaptive right shift at altitude.
explanation_incorrect.D: Fetal hemoglobin (alpha2-gamma2) binds 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate poorly and therefore has a higher oxygen affinity with a left-shifted curve; an increased HbF fraction would not produce a higher P50 in an adult.
explanation_incorrect.E: Oxidation of heme iron to Fe3+ creates methemoglobin, which cannot bind oxygen and left shifts the dissociation curve of the remaining ferrous hemes, causing cyanosis rather than an adaptive right shift.

educationalObjective: Increased erythrocyte 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate at high altitude right-shifts the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve and enhances oxygen unloading to tissues.
